title: A refused stage document reaches the browser as a 200 and an opaque digest
statement: Under `next build` + `next start`, when the restricted compiler throws for a document rendered inside a `<Suspense>` boundary, the response is HTTP 200 — the shell having already streamed — and the boundary's slot resolves to a React error digest with no message, path or position. The compiler's diagnostic exists but does not reach the page.
notes: ⚠️ THE STAGE VIEW MUST CATCH THE REJECTION, not let it throw. Rendering `<Content />` and trusting the compiler to have refused is enough for SAFETY — nothing forbidden executes — and not enough for LEGIBILITY, which is the half DEC-0022 makes a rule: an operator sees a blank region and a success status. ⚠️ It also means a 200 is not evidence a document rendered. Any acceptance check on the stage view must assert an application-owned marker, exactly as the route smoke check already does for the same reason.
